one_liner: Infosys helps large companies around the world run and modernize their technology — building software, managing IT systems, and now adding AI tools — in exchange for long-term service contracts.

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.description: Banking, capital markets and insurance clients; Infosys's largest and most profitable vertical, spanning core banking modernization, payments, and digital transformation.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.description: Discrete and process manufacturers (auto, aerospace, industrials) using Infosys for engineering services, supply-chain digitization and ERP/SAP work.

segments.name: Energy, Utilities, Resources & Services
segments.description: Oil & gas, utilities, mining and services clients adopting cloud, sustainability and grid/asset-management digital solutions.

segments.name: Retail
segments.description: Retail and consumer packaged goods clients for e-commerce platforms, digital commerce, and supply-chain/customer-experience services.

segments.name: Communication
segments.description: Telecom, media and entertainment companies for network transformation, OSS/BSS modernization and customer-experience platforms.

segments.name: Hi-Tech
segments.description: Technology and software companies outsourcing product engineering, QA, and platform support to Infosys.

segments.name: Life Sciences
segments.description: Pharma, healthcare and life-sciences firms using Infosys for R&D IT, regulatory and digital health services.

segments.name: All Other Segments (incl. consulting, EdgeVerve/platforms, public services)
segments.description: Residual industry verticals (public sector, utilities subsegments) plus platform/product revenue (Finacle, EdgeVerve, Topaz) bundled into consolidated reporting; ensures segments sum to total consolidated revenue including subsidiaries.

unit_drivers.name: Billable headcount
unit_drivers.note: Infosys discloses total employee count each quarter; most are billable IT consultants — the core 'volume' driver of revenue.

unit_drivers.name: Revenue per employee
unit_drivers.note: Derived from FY2026 revenue (~₹178,650 cr) divided by ~317k headcount; proxies for pricing and productivity (akin to 'price per unit').

unit_drivers.name: Utilization rate
unit_drivers.note: Infosys reports utilization (ex-trainees) around 85-88% historically; higher utilization directly lifts margin without needing more headcount.

unit_drivers.name: Attrition rate
unit_drivers.note: Talent attrition affects delivery cost and bench strength; Infosys discloses this quarterly as a leading indicator of wage inflation and margin pressure.

unit_drivers.name: Large deal Total Contract Value (TCV) signed
unit_drivers.note: Infosys reports large-deal TCV each quarter; a forward indicator of revenue growth and client concentration/mix.

addressable_market: Global IT services and digital engineering outsourcing market, estimated at roughly $1.3-1.5 trillion annually (Gartner/IDC-type estimates), spanning application services, infrastructure management, consulting, and emerging AI-led transformation work; Infosys competes for a slice of enterprise IT budgets that are shifting from legacy maintenance toward cloud, data and generative-AI spend.
competitive_position: Infosys is one of the top-tier global IT services majors (alongside TCS, Accenture, Cognizant, Wipro, HCLTech), with roughly $19-20bn in annual revenue giving it a mid-single-digit percentage share of the addressable outsourcing market; its moat rests on scale, deep vertical domain expertise (especially BFSI), reusable platforms (Finacle, Cobalt, Topaz) and long-tenured client relationships, though the business remains largely a people-and-process commodity service vulnerable to price competition and talent-based delivery economics.
key_risks: Slower discretionary IT spending in key markets (US/Europe BFSI, retail) during macro slowdowns could compress growth and utilization-driven margins.

Generative AI could both disrupt traditional staff-augmentation pricing (fewer billable hours needed per project) and create new competitive entrants, pressuring long-term revenue-per-employee economics.
Wage inflation, rising attrition, or visa/immigration policy shifts in the US (a major revenue market) could raise delivery costs and compress the already thin 20-21% operating margin.
industry_reason: Infosys earns its profit through large-scale, people-intensive IT consulting, outsourcing and systems-integration contracts rather than owning software IP or hardware — the same economic model as the 196-firm 'Computer Services' peer group (IT services/outsourcing), whose ~17% average operating margin is close to Infosys's own 20-21%, making it a much better fit than product-software or hardware-oriented groups.
